1.explanation:
1. Dropdown.js – this is where the component’s props are defined and passed into Downshift and the input field. We need to add a readOnly prop, prevent opening the menu when readOnly is true, and pass the attribute down to the underlying <input> as readOnly.
2. Dropdown.stories.js – storybook needs a new story and controls for readOnly so designers and consumers can toggle and copy/paste a fully configured example.
3. __tests__/Dropdown-test.js – add RTL unit tests that assert the rendered DOM includes a read-only class or attribute and that keyboard/mouse events don’t open the menu in read-only mode.
4. _dropdown.scss – introduce a CSS modifier (e.g. &.bx--dropdown--readonly) to gray out borders/text and suppress hover/active styles per the design specs.
5. Dropdown-test.e2e.js – end-to-end test to verify that clicking or pressing Enter on the dropdown does not open the list when readOnly is set, ensuring we’ve disabled interactive behavior in a real browser environment.
1.bug_scenario: In the current implementation of the React Dropdown component, passing a readOnly={true} prop does not prevent user interaction, nor does it apply any distinct ‘read-only’ styles. The menu can still open, items can be selected, and the control looks and behaves identically to the enabled component. The acceptance criteria call for a proper read-only mode: non-interactive, styled appropriately, storybook controls, a default story, and RTL tests verifying the read-only class.

2.explanation: Dropdown.js needs the readOnly prop added to propTypes/defaultProps, logic updated so that when readOnly is true the menu won’t open and the toggle icon is disabled. Dropdown.stories.js must expose readOnly in the controls panel and include a default readOnly story for easy copy/paste. Dropdown-test.js (RTL unit tests) should verify that the component gains the appropriate read-only class and that clicking does nothing. Dropdown-test.e2e.js should add an end-to-end scenario confirming the user cannot open the menu when readOnly. Finally, the SCSS module (_dropdown.scss) must define styling for the new read-only state (e.g. placeholder text color, disabled icon color, pointer-events:none, etc.).
2.bug_scenario: When a consumer passes the new readOnly prop (e.g. <Dropdown readOnly>), the Dropdown should render in a non-interactive, read-only state (using placeholder styling, disabling the toggle icon, preventing the menu from opening, etc.). Currently the component ignores readOnly entirely—clicking still opens the menu, styling is unchanged, and there’s no readOnly story or test coverage.
